title: Disambiguate hierarchy-adjacent module and CLI naming
description:
Resolve the four naming collisions around hierarchy so each name maps to one concept: module placement for the type taxonomy, the init-preset module's mixed responsibilities, the overloaded "divergence" CLI surface, and the duplicated `Scope` identifier.

## Background

Four distinct concepts share names today: (1) `type_hierarchy.rs` (pure type-label taxonomy, src root) collides with `graph/hierarchy.rs` (DAG resolution) — the taxonomy and its `HierarchyConfig` belong under `domain/` with a distinct name; (2) `hierarchy_templates.rs` mixes pure init-preset data with `get_hierarchy_config` (`hierarchy_templates.rs:386-408`), a loader that performs storage I/O from a root module; (3) "divergence" means membership-vs-DAG mismatch in `jit query divergence` but git branch drift in `jit validate --divergence` (`validate.rs:1635`); (4) `domain::item::Scope` and `validation::rules::Scope` are two unrelated types with one identifier, imported side by side in `validation/graph.rs`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-1: The type-taxonomy module lives under `domain/` with a name distinct from `graph/hierarchy`, and `HierarchyConfig` moves with it; `graph/` still depends only on pure modules.
- [hard] REQ-2: The storage-reading config loader is relocated to the config/command layer; the preset module holds pure preset data only.
- [hard] REQ-3: The branch-drift validate flag has a name that cannot be confused with membership divergence; the old spelling produces a hint naming the new flag, and help text plus docs distinguish the two concepts.
- [hard] REQ-4: Exactly one type named `Scope` exists in the crate; the other is renamed to state what it scopes.
- [hard] REQ-5: Architecture narrative (CLAUDE.md, docs) reflects the new module locations, stating current structure only.

## Notes

Pure renames and moves; no behavior change. Land as mechanical commits (move, then rename) so review can verify equivalence.
